items.title: Closed-Then-Reposted Requisition Motif
items.content:
# Closed-Then-Reposted Requisition Motif

A candidate completes multiple late-stage interviews, is rejected with a generic message, and sees the identical role reposted weeks later.

### Trigger Rule
The role is closed and the candidate rejected, and a materially similar listing is publicly reopened within 60 days.

### What this Establishes
- The interviewed pool did not meet the requisition's requirements or target profile, or the search criteria changed mid-process.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the original job listing was fake or a ghost job.
- Does not establish that the candidate was intentionally misled.
items.summary: A candidate completes multiple late-stage interviews, is rejected with a generic message, and sees the identical role reposted weeks later.
items.trigger_rule: The role is closed and the candidate rejected, and a materially similar listing is publicly reopened within 60 days.
establishes: The interviewed pool did not meet the requisition's requirements or target profile, or the search criteria changed mid-process.
non_inferences: Does not establish that the original job listing was fake or a ghost job.
Does not establish that the candidate was intentionally misled.

specimens.label: The sequence, as recorded

lines.text: Applied — req #4471
Recruiter screen — passed
Technical panel — passed
Final round with hiring manager — completed
Rejected — generic template, no specifics given
req #4471 visible on the careers page again, text unchanged

specimens.reading: Late-stage progress, a contentless rejection, and the same requisition number back on the board. The sequence is the observation; its cause is not in the sequence.

specimens.label: The question that splits the branches

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: I saw req #4471 listed again. Is this a new opening on the team, or the same one?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Same requisition. We restarted the search with a revised profile after the first round of interviews.

specimens.reading: A revised profile, an automated refresh and a genuinely new headcount are three different mechanisms with one appearance. This is the question that tells them apart.

perspectives.sees: A generic rejection after a final round, and the same requisition number back on the careers page weeks later with the text unchanged.
perspectives.reads: Either the profile was revised, or the platform refreshed the listing, or the headcount is new — and the sequence on its own does not separate them.
perspectives.does: Asks whether the listing is the same requisition, and records the dates and the answer before deciding whether to reapply.

perspectives.sees: The requisition record moving from closed back to open with a revised profile, and a rejection template that is the same for every candidate at that stage.
perspectives.reads: This is one continuous search that changed shape, not two openings.
perspectives.does: Sends the standard wording, since a specific reason given at the close of one round can be quoted back at the next, and states the restart when a candidate asks directly.

perspectives.sees: Two finalists at the end of a loop, and the work the role exists to absorb still uncovered.
perspectives.reads: A loop that ended without a hire is information about the profile, and the profile is the part of this the manager controls.
perspectives.does: Rewrites the requirements and restarts the search on the same requisition, because a new requisition would go back through funding.

perspectives.sees: A requisition whose status returned to open, and a scheduled refresh that pushes open listings back out to aggregators with a current date.
perspectives.reads: An open requisition is a listing to distribute; the refresh reads the status field and not the history behind it.
perspectives.does: Republishes under the original identifier and stamps the posting with today's date, which is the default behaviour for any open requisition.

items.title: Compensation Double Bind
items.content:
# Compensation Double Bind

The candidate has to name a compensation expectation first: a high number ends the process, and a low one lowers the level the candidate is assessed at.

### Trigger Rule
The candidate is asked for a compensation number before the band for the role is stated, and the band is not stated in return.

### What this Establishes
- An information asymmetry works as an uncalibrated filter before technical merit is assessed.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the employer has an unlimited budget, or that any of this is malicious.
items.summary: The candidate has to name a compensation expectation first: a high number ends the process, and a low one lowers the level the candidate is assessed at.
items.trigger_rule: The candidate is asked for a compensation number before the band for the role is stated, and the band is not stated in return.
establishes: An information asymmetry works as an uncalibrated filter before technical merit is assessed.
non_inferences: Does not establish that the employer has an unlimited budget, or that any of this is malicious.

specimens.label: The asymmetry, in four messages

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Before we go further — what are your compensation expectations?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Happy to discuss. What is the band for the role?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: We prefer to hear the candidate number first so we can match it to the right level.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood. My expectation is in the range of 85–95k.

specimens.reading: The number is required from one side and withheld by the other, and it is collected before the level is fixed. Both outcomes below follow from that ordering.

specimens.label: The two branches
specimens.context: the same question, two candidates, one week

lines.text: Quoted 95k — We are not able to proceed; the expectation is outside the range we have for this role.
Quoted 70k — Good news, we would like to move ahead. Based on the conversation we are looking at this as a mid-level hire rather than senior.

specimens.reading: A high number ends the process and a low one moves the level. There is no answer that leaves both the process and the grade untouched — which is what makes it a bind rather than a negotiation.

perspectives.sees: A request for a compensation expectation at the screen, and a band that is not stated in return.
perspectives.reads: The number is collected before the level is fixed, so it is an input to the level rather than an answer to it.
perspectives.does: Names a range without the band, without the level, and without knowing how many others in the pipeline have already named one.

perspectives.sees: A screening form with an expectations field that has to be filled before the candidate moves to the panel, and disclosure rules for the band that are set elsewhere.
perspectives.reads: The number is the cheapest available check on whether the process is viable, before panel time is spent on it.
perspectives.does: Asks for the number first and records it in the field, and says about the band exactly what is permitted at this stage.

perspectives.sees: A band per level and a rule about what may be said about it, both reviewed on a cycle measured in quarters.
perspectives.reads: A stated expectation is the input that places a candidate on the grid; a band stated first becomes the floor of every negotiation that follows.
perspectives.does: Publishes the band where a disclosure rule requires it and not elsewhere, and keeps levelling a decision separate from the number.

perspectives.sees: Postings in covered jurisdictions, which either carry a band or do not.
perspectives.reads: A published band is measurable and enforceable; the level a candidate will be assessed at is neither.
perspectives.does: Requires the band in the posting, which closes one branch of the bind and leaves the levelling branch untouched.

items.title: Experience-Age Impossibility
items.content:
# Experience-Age Impossibility

A requisition requires more years of hands-on experience with a specific framework or tool than that technology has existed in the open-source ecosystem.

### Trigger Rule
Job description or automated screen requires X years of experience where X > technology_age.

### What this Establishes
- The job description was written without technical review, from a copied template whose thresholds run as automated gating rules.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the technical team is incompetent, only that the HR screening pipeline has no technical review.
items.summary: A requisition requires more years of hands-on experience with a specific framework or tool than that technology has existed in the open-source ecosystem.
items.trigger_rule: Job description or automated screen requires X years of experience where X > technology_age.
establishes: The job description was written without technical review, from a copied template whose thresholds run as automated gating rules.
non_inferences: Does not establish that the technical team is incompetent, only that the HR screening pipeline has no technical review.

specimens.label: The requirement, as published
specimens.subject: Senior Platform Engineer — requirements

lines.text: 7+ years of production experience with Kubernetes.
5+ years with a framework first released three years ago.
Screening is automated: applications below the stated year counts are filtered before human review.

specimens.reading: This is checkable against a release date, which makes it one of the few claims in hiring that can simply be false rather than debatable.

specimens.label: What the filter did with it

lines.text: Application submitted
Rule: years_with_framework >= 5 — candidate value 3 — FAIL
Status: Rejected — does not meet minimum criteria

specimens.reading: No one decided anything about this candidate. An impossible threshold was copied into a rule and the rule ran.

perspectives.sees: A posting requiring more years with a framework than the framework has existed, and a rejection minutes after submitting, outside working hours.
perspectives.reads: The threshold is checkable against a release date, which makes this one of the few claims in a posting that can be false rather than arguable.
perspectives.does: Keeps the posting text and the time of the rejection, which can be set against the release date; the requirement itself reaches nobody who could rewrite it.

perspectives.sees: A draft posting assembled from the template of a previous requisition, reviewed for the part that describes the team's work.
perspectives.reads: Years of experience is a shorthand for depth, and in the draft that figure carries less weight than the description of the role.
perspectives.does: Approves the draft and returns to the delivery the requisition exists to cover; the number reaches a screening rule without passing a technical review.

perspectives.sees: A configured knockout rule comparing a parsed year count against a threshold the customer entered.
perspectives.reads: A value below the threshold is a fail; whether the threshold is reachable at all is not a property the rule can evaluate.
perspectives.does: Rejects at submission and emits the standard does-not-meet-minimum-criteria notice, in seconds, at whatever hour it arrives.

items.title: Seniority Double Bind
items.content:
# Seniority Double Bind

The same candidate is rejected as overqualified for junior and mid-level roles and as underqualified, or not specialised enough, for staff and leadership roles.

### Trigger Rule
The candidate is rejected as overqualified at level N and as short on depth at level N+1 within the same market cycle.

### What this Establishes
- The candidate falls into a gap between evaluation tiers, where the compensation and experience expected match neither tier.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the candidate lacks market value.
- Does not establish malice or coordinated collusion between employers.
items.summary: The same candidate is rejected as overqualified for junior and mid-level roles and as underqualified, or not specialised enough, for staff and leadership roles.
items.trigger_rule: The candidate is rejected as overqualified at level N and as short on depth at level N+1 within the same market cycle.
establishes: The candidate falls into a gap between evaluation tiers, where the compensation and experience expected match neither tier.
non_inferences: Does not establish that the candidate lacks market value.
Does not establish malice or coordinated collusion between employers.

specimens.label: Two rejections, six weeks apart
specimens.context: same candidate, same market, adjacent levels

lines.text: 12 Feb — Senior Backend Engineer (level 4). Your experience sits above the band scoped for this role and we were concerned it would not hold your interest.
26 Mar — Staff Engineer (level 5). The panel felt the depth of platform ownership was not yet at staff scope; we would look for a broader track record of org-wide impact.
Both roles: same city, same domain, same six-week window.

specimens.reading: Neither message is unreasonable on its own. Put next to each other they describe a candidate who is above one level and below the next, with nothing in between open.

specimens.label: What the pair does and does not establish

lines.text: Established: two rejections, two stated grounds, two adjacent levels, one market cycle.

Not established: that either judgement was wrong, that the two employers coordinated, or that the candidate is unhireable. The motif is a property of the level grid, not of the person moving through it.

specimens.reading: The pattern is worth naming precisely because each half is defensible. The trap is structural, which is also why no single conversation can argue it away.

perspectives.sees: Two rejections inside one market cycle: one saying the experience sits above the band scoped for the role, one saying the depth is not yet at the next level's scope.
perspectives.reads: Together the two messages describe a person who is above one rung and below the next, with nothing open in between.
perspectives.does: Applies at both levels at once and shifts what the CV emphasises depending on which rung the posting names.

perspectives.sees: A profile whose years and previous scope sit above the band approved for the requisition being screened.
perspectives.reads: An expectation above the band reads as an offer that will not close, and the level of the requisition is fixed before the screen begins.
perspectives.does: Closes the application against this requisition and writes the rejection in terms of fit with the level it was opened at.

perspectives.sees: A candidate in a staff-level round, assessed against the scope the panel has agreed for that level: ownership across an organisation rather than a team.
perspectives.reads: A track record that has not yet run at that scope is a risk that lands on the person who makes the hire.
perspectives.does: Records a not-at-this-level decision and leaves the requisition open: a bad hire carries a name and a search still running does not.

perspectives.sees: A levelling grid in which every level has a band and the bands are contiguous, and requisitions that are each opened at a single level.
perspectives.reads: A candidate above one band and below the next is a mismatch between a person and a particular requisition, not a gap in the grid; the grid is what makes offers consistent across every hire.
perspectives.does: Holds the grid steady through the cycle and approves requisitions at one level, because the level is the unit finance funds.
